pageInfo.subtitle: Master the art of outlining chords and creating melodic lines with harmonic clarity through arpeggio-based improvisation.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Arpeggios are the skeleton of harmony made melodic. Learn to outline chord changes with clarity and sophistication, creating melodic lines that highlight the harmonic structure of your solos.

items.text: Chord Definition: Arpeggios clearly outline underlying harmony
Strong Foundation: Chord tones are always harmonically safe
Professional Sound: Essential for jazz and sophisticated playing
Melodic Structure: Provides framework for melodic development
Chord Changes: Outline each chord as harmony changes
Complex Harmony: Navigate difficult chord progressions
Strong Beats: Land on chord tones on important beats
Harmonic Clarity: When you want to highlight the harmony

exercises.title: Basic Triads
exercises.description: Three-note chords that outline fundamental harmonic structures. Includes: Major Triad (1-3-5), Minor Triad (1-♭3-5), Diminished Triad (1-♭3-♭5), Augmented Triad (1-3-♯5). Characteristics: Clear harmonic outline, easy to hear chord changes, fundamental building blocks.

practiceNotes.title: Best For
practiceNotes.text: Country music, Folk, Basic rock, Classical. These triads are the fundamental building blocks of all arpeggio-based improvisation.

exercises.title: Seventh Chords
exercises.description: Four-note arpeggios that add harmonic sophistication and jazz flavor. Includes: Major 7th (1-3-5-7), Dominant 7th (1-3-5-♭7), Minor 7th (1-♭3-5-♭7), Half-Diminished (1-♭3-♭5-♭7). Characteristics: Rich harmonic color, jazz standard vocabulary, smooth voice leading.

practiceNotes.title: Best For
practiceNotes.text: Jazz, Blues, R&B, Sophisticated pop. Seventh chord arpeggios are the core vocabulary for jazz and blues improvisation.

exercises.title: Extended Chords
exercises.description: Complex arpeggios that include 9ths, 11ths, and 13ths for modern sounds. Includes: Major 9th, Minor 9th, Dominant 13th, Minor 11th, Major 7#11. Characteristics: Modern harmonic color, complex but beautiful, professional sound.

practiceNotes.title: Best For
practiceNotes.text: Jazz fusion, Contemporary jazz, Modern pop, Film music. Extended arpeggios create the sophisticated sounds heard in professional recordings.

exercises.title: Altered Dominants
exercises.description: Modified dominant arpeggios that create tension and sophisticated resolution. Includes: 7♭5, 7♯5, 7♭9, 7♯9, 7alt (♭9♯9♯11♭13). Characteristics: Maximum tension, jazz sophistication, strong resolution tendency.

practiceNotes.title: Best For
practiceNotes.text: Bebop, Modern jazz, Fusion, Advanced improvisation. Altered dominants are the hallmark of advanced jazz improvisation.

exercises.title: Chord Outlining
exercises.description: Play arpeggio notes to clearly define the underlying harmony. Land on chord tones on strong beats, especially chord changes. Over Cmaj7-Am7-Dm7-G7, play respective arpeggio tones.

practiceNotes.title: Musical Effect
practiceNotes.text: Creates harmonic clarity and professional sound. This is the most fundamental arpeggio application technique.

exercises.title: Connecting Arpeggios
exercises.description: Link arpeggios smoothly through chord progressions. Use common tones and stepwise motion between arpeggios. Connect C major to A minor via shared tones (C and E).

practiceNotes.title: Musical Effect
practiceNotes.text: Smooth voice leading and flowing melodic lines. The key to professional-sounding arpeggio improvisation.

exercises.title: Arpeggio Patterns
exercises.description: Use recurring patterns within arpeggios for rhythmic interest. Play arpeggios in 3rds, 4ths, or skip patterns. Example patterns: 1-3-5-7-5-3 or 1-5-3-7.

practiceNotes.title: Musical Effect
practiceNotes.text: Adds structure and memorability to lines. Patterns give your improvisation rhythmic drive and coherence.

exercises.title: Scale-Arpeggio Integration
exercises.description: Combine arpeggios with scale passages for variety. Use arpeggios for chord tones, scales for passing tones. Arpeggio on beats 1&3, scalar fills on beats 2&4.

practiceNotes.title: Musical Effect
practiceNotes.text: Balances harmonic clarity with melodic flow. This is the approach used by most professional improvisers.

exercises.title: Rhythmic Displacement
exercises.description: Play arpeggios with different rhythmic groupings. Use triplets, quintuplets, or syncopated rhythms. Play 4-note arpeggio as triplet grouping for rhythmic tension.

practiceNotes.title: Musical Effect
practiceNotes.text: Creates rhythmic sophistication and interest. Rhythmic displacement is a hallmark of advanced arpeggio improvisation.

exercises.title: Arpeggio Foundation
exercises.description: Build solid arpeggio technique across the fretboard. Steps: 1. Practice major and minor triads in multiple positions. 2. Play arpeggios ascending and descending. 3. Use alternate picking for clean articulation. 4. Practice with metronome at various tempos. 5. Memorize arpeggio shapes without looking.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Focus on clean, even notes rather than speed. Start at a comfortable tempo and gradually increase.

exercises.title: Chord Progression Mapping
exercises.description: Learn to play appropriate arpeggios over chord changes. Steps: 1. Choose a simple progression (I-vi-IV-V). 2. Identify the correct arpeggio for each chord. 3. Practice each arpeggio separately. 4. Connect arpeggios through the progression. 5. Add scalar passages between chord tones.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Listen for how arpeggios outline the harmony. Focus on smooth transitions between chords.

exercises.title: Jazz Standard Application
exercises.description: Apply arpeggios to real jazz standards. Steps: 1. Choose a simple jazz standard (Autumn Leaves). 2. Analyze the chord progression. 3. Practice appropriate arpeggios for each chord. 4. Work on smooth voice leading between chords. 5. Add rhythmic and melodic variations.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Start slowly and focus on harmonic accuracy. The goal is clean, clear arpeggio movement through changes.

exercises.title: Advanced Arpeggio Integration
exercises.description: Combine multiple arpeggio concepts in improvisation. Steps: 1. Practice extended and altered arpeggios. 2. Work on rapid arpeggio sequences. 3. Combine with chromatic approach tones. 4. Practice over complex jazz progressions. 5. Record and analyze harmonic accuracy.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Advanced arpeggios require significant practice to sound musical. Record yourself and listen back critically.

items.title: Phase 1: Technical (10 mins)
items: Practice basic triads in multiple positions

items.title: Phase 2: Harmonic (15 mins)
items: Work on voice leading between chords

items.title: Famous Arpeggio Masters
items: Wes Montgomery: Smooth arpeggio lines with octave technique - fluid arpeggios that outline complex jazz harmony
Pat Metheny: Wide interval arpeggios with modern extensions - uses extended arpeggios for contemporary jazz sounds
Allan Holdsworth: Rapid legato arpeggios with complex harmony - lightning-fast arpeggios through dense chord changes
George Benson: R&B influenced arpeggios with strong groove - combines technical arpeggio work with strong rhythmic feel

journeySection.title: Continue Your Improvisation Journey
journeySection.description: Arpeggio mastery is essential for sophisticated improvisation. Explore these related topics to deepen your harmonic understanding.
